Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 11:169: And in the Zohar (Parashat Naso, page 145b), they explained on this verse that whoever merits fear merits humility and piety - Rabbi Elazar said, whoever has fear, humility, and piety in him has the sum of all in him. And he said there that "yerei'av" [those who fear Him] refers to the sum of male and female, which is "Adam" - and whoever joins male and female is called "Adam," and then he fears sin, and not only that, but humility rests in him, and not only that, but Chesed rests in him. And whoever is not found [united as] male and female has neither fear nor humility nor piety - and therefore he is called "Adam," the sum of all; and since he is called "Adam," Chesed rests in him, as it is written (Psalms 89:3), "I have said, the world shall be built with kindness," and so on - to this point, relevant here. It seems to me that his words concerning "Adam" may be understood by what is explained in the Zohar (Parashat Bereshit, page 34b) concerning the division of the letters of "Adam" - see there - and by this the rest of the discourse is understood.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 11:170: And when a person holds fast to all the attributes of Chesed mentioned, and to the other attributes mentioned in the discourse, the holy spirit will rest upon him. And it seems to me that this is what they said, of blessed memory (Bava Batra 25b): whoever wishes to become wise should turn southward - meaning, whoever wishes to merit the attribute of wisdom must hold fast to the attribute of Chesed, called "south," for Chesed is the throne for Chochmah, and by holding fast to the attributes of Chesed, he will certainly merit the Chochmah that is above it.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 11:171: And in Tanna D'Vei Eliyahu, concerning meriting the holy spirit, he said, in these words, in the Yalkut (Judges, section 42, page 9b), on the verse "and Deborah, a woman, a prophetess" (Judges 4:4): what was the nature of Deborah, that she prophesied over Israel and judged them, when Pinchas the son of Elazar was still living? I call heaven and earth to witness for me: whether gentile or Jew, whether man or woman, whether slave or maidservant, according to a person's deeds, the holy spirit rests upon him. And the rest of his words, concerning the matter of "Lapidot," still need to be copied.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 12:1: We have seen fit, in this chapter, to explain that among the levels a person reaches to become a lover and pious one, he must acquire three attributes: the first, trust [bitachon]; the second, faith [emunah]; the third, joy [simchah]. Trust, as it is said (Psalms 32:10), "but he who trusts in the LORD, kindness shall surround him."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 12:2: Faith - Abraham our father, peace be upon him, is the head of the believers, as it is said (Genesis 15:6), "and he believed in the LORD," and this is the word "emunah" first mentioned in the Torah; and so it is written in Deuteronomy (7:9), "the faithful God, who keeps the covenant and kindness," and likewise (Deuteronomy 32:4), "a God of faithfulness, and without iniquity."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 12:3: And further our Rabbis, of blessed memory, said in Midrash Shir HaShirim (4:20 [sic]), and likewise in Midrash Shemot Rabbah, on the verse "then sang," in these words: another interpretation, "look [tashuri] from the top of Amanah" (Song of Songs 4:8) - this is Abraham, of whom it is written, "and he believed [ve-he'emin] in the LORD." "From the top of Senir" - this is Isaac; "and Hermon" - this is Jacob - to this point, relevant here.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 12:4: And so they explained in the Tikkunim (page 5a) concerning "and He shall be the faith [emunat] of your times" (Isaiah 33:6): that "Emunah" is Seder Zera'im [an order of the Mishnah, homiletically] in Chesed, and he says, "Emunah" is the supernal Mother, from the side of Chesed, in whom is the Shema, which is Emunah - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 12:5: Joy - as explained in Parashat Vayikra (Zohar, page 8a), that the priest is the one who gladdens, and of him it is said (Psalms 100:2), "serve the LORD with joy."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 12:6: And let us return to explain each and every one of these on its own, and through this the matter of complete love will be explained to you. Trust is a person's rest and tranquility from worry over the thing he fears, when he considers that thing on which he relies and leans as a shield, a buckler, and a fortified wall - and then he is secure and does not fear that former dread, as he says (Deuteronomy 28:52), "the fortified [walls] in which you trust." And the parable for this: the poor man trusts his heart in the rich man to support him with his charity; so too the mighty man in his might, and the wise man in his wisdom.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 12:7: And because all these things are from Him, blessed be He - I mean, from His supernal attributes toward us, for He and His attributes are all one - therefore King David, peace be upon him, said (Psalms 31:15), "but I trusted in You, O LORD," "and I trusted in Your kindness" (ibid. 13:6), "in this I trust" (ibid. 27:3), "my heart trusted in Him, and I was helped" (ibid. 28:7), "trust in Him, and He will act" (ibid. 37:5) - and "in Him" here is like "cast your burden upon the LORD" (ibid. 55:23), which they explained in the Zohar (Parashat Acharei, page 79b) as referring to the things that depend on mazal [fortune], which is "al" [upon]. "I trusted in the kindness of God," and so on (ibid. 52:10); "in God I have trusted, I will not fear" (ibid. 56:5); "happy is the man who trusts in You," and so on (ibid. 84:13); "his heart is steadfast, trusting in the LORD" (ibid. 112:7); "in the fear of the LORD is strong confidence," and so on (Proverbs 14:26); "and he who trusts in the LORD, happy is he" (ibid. 16:20); and so "and he who trusts in the LORD shall be made fat" (ibid. 28:25) - behold, from these verses the place of trust will be explained to you, if you are proficient in the appellations of the attributes explained in the Zohar.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 12:8: And the pious author of Chovot HaLevavot (Gate of Trust, chapter 3) wrote that the premises through which trust is completed for a person are these: first, that he believe that the Creator, blessed be He, has more mercy on a person than any other one who has mercy, and all mercy and compassion shown to him by anyone else are all from God's mercy and compassion, as it is said (Psalms 103:8), "the LORD is merciful and gracious," and it says (Deuteronomy 13:18), "and give you mercy, and have compassion upon you, and multiply you."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 12:9: And the second, that the modes of a person's benefit are not hidden from the Creator, blessed be He, because He devised the root of man, his form, his constitution, and the order of his composition - He is the Wise One who knows his affairs, his benefits, his harms, and what is good for him both in his world and in his end, as it is written (Isaiah 48:17), "I am the LORD your God, who teaches you to profit, who leads you by the way you should go."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 12:10: And the third, that the Creator, blessed be He, is mighty, not to be overcome, in what He desires, as it is written (Job 9:4), "wise in heart, and mighty in strength," and His word is decreed above every other thing, and none can reverse His judgment, as it is written, "all that He desired, He has done," and so on, and it says (Isaiah 55:11), "so shall My word be that goes forth from My mouth; it shall not return to Me void." And therefore there is none who can prevent Him from fulfilling the request of one who trusts in Him - for if He were weak, trust would not be complete regarding Him.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 12:11: And the fourth, that He knows the modes of benefit of the one who trusts, and what is good for him is not hidden from Him, whether in secret or in the open, and He watches over the conduct of all people; He does not abandon them nor is He hidden from them, and nothing of theirs is concealed from Him, as it is written (Psalms 121:3-4), "behold, He who keeps Israel shall neither slumber nor sleep," and it says (Isaiah 40:27), "why do you say, O Jacob, and speak, O Israel, my way is hidden from the LORD," and so on, "have you not known? have you not heard? the everlasting God," and so on.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 12:12: And the fifth, that He is uniquely devoted to the conduct of the one who trusts in Him, from the beginning of his existence, through his growth, his infancy, his youth, and his old age, to the end of his affairs, as it is written (Deuteronomy 32:6), "is not He your father who acquired you? He made you and established you," and it says (Psalms 22:10), "for You took me out of the womb; You made me trust while on my mother's breasts. I was cast upon You from the womb; from my mother's belly You have been my God," and it says (Job 10:10), "have You not poured me out like milk," and so on.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 12:13: And the sixth, that the affairs of the one who trusts are given into His hand - no person can harm him or benefit him, or push away harm from him, except through His power, blessed be He - and he is like an imprisoned servant, who is in a pit, in the net of his master. And when a person feels that no created being can benefit or harm him except by permission of the Creator, blessed be He, his heart shall turn from fearing them and shall trust in the Creator, blessed be He, as it is written (Psalms 146:3), "do not trust in princes," and so on, "happy is he whose help is the God of Jacob, whose hope is in the LORD his God." And it says (Jeremiah 17:5), "cursed is the man who trusts in man," and so on (ibid. 17:7), "blessed is the man who trusts in the LORD."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 12:14: And the seventh, that he know that the One in whom he trusts is the ultimate in generosity and kindness, toward whoever is deserving and whoever is not deserving, and His generosity is constant and His kindness continuous - it is never cut off nor ceases - and a person is obligated in service to Him for the abundant kindness and goodness he received from Him, without his having deserved it or any prior kindness having preceded it, as He says (Job 41:3), "who has preceded Me, that I should repay him?" And as King David, peace be upon him, said (Psalms 40:6), "many things have You done, O LORD my God, Your wonders and Your thoughts toward us," and so on, and it says (ibid. 145:9), "the LORD is good to all, and His mercies are over all His works," and it says (ibid. 136:25), "who gives food to all flesh, for His kindness endures forever," and it says (ibid. 145:16), "You open Your hand, and satisfy the desire of every living thing."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 12:15: And reason dictates that when these seven matters are combined in the Creator, blessed be He, a person's trust in Him should be strengthened, and he should give himself over to Him and not suspect His judgment, nor grow angry at His choice - as King David, peace be upon him, said (Psalms 116:3-4), "trouble and sorrow I found, and I called upon the name of the LORD" - to this point is the summary of his words.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 12:16: And when you examine these seven matters mentioned, you will find that all these actions are unique to the attribute of Chesed, blessed be He, and especially to the matter of constant providence and the kindnesses that never cease, which are unique to the "open eye" of Arich [Anpin], as it is written in the Idra of Naso (pages 129-130), that this eye neither slumbers nor sleeps, and watches constantly. And it says there that it watches over everything, and everything is sustained through it; and it further says, and this eye is the sustaining of everything - and of this it is written (Proverbs 22:9), "he who has a good eye shall be blessed [yevorach]" - do not read "yevorach" but "yevarech" [shall bless] - for this is called "a good eye," and from it everything is blessed.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 12:17: And the other actions mentioned, such as (Psalms 22:10), "for You took me out of the womb; You made me trust while on my mother's breasts" - these actions are attributed to the lower Chesed, called "Atah" - "Atah" is the priest forever, and likewise "from my mother's belly, Atah [You have been] my God." And there is a providence attributed to the lower Chesed, for "ra'iyah" [sight] belongs to the right, as explained in the Tikkunim (page 122a), and they gave "the face of a lion" as the sign for the right, and "re'iyah" [sight] is [an anagram of] "aryeh" [lion]. However, this lower providence, which is in the lower eye, sometimes ceases, and therefore the Psalmist said (ibid. 44:24), "awake, why do You sleep, O LORD?" But the supernal providence never ceases.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 12:18: And therefore, wherever trust is found, it is the aspect of Chesed spreading through all the attributes, and therefore we find trust in supernal Chesed, as it says (ibid. 21:8), "for the king trusts in the LORD, and through the kindness of the Most High he shall not be moved." And even the trust mentioned concerning "Elohim," as he says (ibid. 56:5), "in God [Elohim] I have trusted, I will not fear," and so on - the intent is toward the aspect of Chesed within Elohim, which is "El" from "Elohim," as he says (ibid. 52:10), "I trusted in the kindness of God [Elohim]" - or the intent is toward the general Chesed within the attribute of Elohim, in such a way that whoever trusts in the LORD is fitting that kindness surround him, for Chesed is what spreads, as explained.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 12:19: And among the conditions of the one who trusts is that he consider and know that the Creator sees his heart, whether his trust in Him is complete or not - for a servant serving before a king of flesh and blood can deceive his heart, but from the Creator, blessed be He, the Fashioner of hearts, nothing is hidden that could deceive Him, as it is written (Psalms 94:11), "the LORD knows the thoughts of man, that they are vanity," and it says (Proverbs 24:12), "does not He who weighs the hearts perceive it?" and it says (2 Chronicles 6:30), "for You alone know the hearts of the children of men." And he should not trust in any person apart from the ability of the Name, as it is written (Jeremiah 17:5), "cursed is the man who trusts in man," and so on, "and whose heart departs from the LORD" - for all the causes that reach him, such as sustenance or his other acquisitions and his healing, are all causes caused by Him, blessed be He, to bring that thing to him. And the pious author of Chovot HaLevavot already gave a parable for this in his book (Gate of Trust, chapter 3), likening it to a water wheel that draws water from the well through the prepared vessels - for if one of them is lacking, the drawing of water fails.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 12:20: Further, I found written a fitting parable for this matter: it is like blind men walking one after another, each placing his hand on his fellow's shoulder, but all are drawn after the first, who sees - and if he should slip away from them, they would all stumble and fall. So it is fitting for a person to think that there is no guide besides Him, blessed be He, the unique One exalted above all, and from Him all the causes and intermediaries are set in motion to bring the desired thing to him - healing through such-and-such a remedy through such-and-such a medicine, and similarly for other worldly matters, like a craft that is a cause for his livelihood - he should not trust in that cause, for if that cause is nullified, his livelihood and sustenance will not be lacking because of it, for the Holy One, blessed be He, will provide his sustenance through another means - like a man splitting wood with an axe: even though the axe cuts the wood, the power does not come from the axe but from the man splitting it, as it is written (Isaiah 10:15), "shall the axe boast itself against him who hews with it?"
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 12:21: And among the matters of trust, the author of Chovot HaLevavot wrote (ibid.) that his providence should be strong and his effort great to fulfill what the Creator obligated him in His service, and to perform His commandments, and to be careful of what He warned him against, so that the Creator agree with him in what he trusts Him for - as they said, of blessed memory (Avot, chapter 2, mishnah 4): do His will as your own will, so that He do your will as His own will; nullify your will before His will, and so on. And Scripture says (Psalms 37:3), "trust in the LORD, and do good; dwell in the land, and feed on faithfulness," and it says (Lamentations 3:25), "the LORD is good to those who wait for Him, to the soul that seeks Him." But whoever trusts in the Creator while rebelling against Him - how foolish he is, and how weak is his understanding and discernment! For you see that whoever is appointed by people over a matter - when he commands him to occupy himself for the sake of his needs, or warns him about his affairs, and he transgresses his command, and it reaches the one who appointed him that he transgressed his command - this becomes a strong cause preventing him from fulfilling what he trusted him for. All the more so one who has transgressed the statutes and commandments of God, which He has promised and testified about, that the hope of the one who trusts in Him shall be disappointed when he rebels against Him, and he is not fit to be called by the name "one who trusts in God" - rather, he is as Scripture says (Job 27:8), "for what is the hope of the flatterer, though he has gained, when God takes away his soul? will God hear his cry," and so on, and it says (Jeremiah 7:9-10), "will you steal, murder," and so on, "and come and stand before Me in this house?" - to this point. And I say that concerning this it is said (Proverbs 14:16), "but the fool rages, and is confident."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 12:22: And so it is fitting that he not trust in his wealth, as it is said (ibid. 11:28), "he who trusts in his riches shall fall" - for everything is from Him, as it is said (1 Chronicles 29:14), "for everything comes from You, and of Your own have we given You."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 12:23: And so among the matters of trust, he should not trust in his good deeds, as though through them he would be saved from the mishaps of the world and bad illnesses - for if so, he would be found consuming his merits - but rather he should trust in His kindness, for his deeds do not suffice to repay the debts owed the Creator upon him, as the pious one elaborated in Chovot HaLevavot (Gate of Trust, chapter 4), that even if his deeds were doubled many times over, they would not suffice to repay even one of the Creator's kindnesses to him. Rather, he should think that just as He, blessed be He, gives sustenance to all creatures and to roots, to beasts, animals, and birds - as they said, of blessed memory (Shabbat 107b), He sits and sustains from the horns of the wild oxen to the eggs of lice - just as He has mercy on these not because of their deeds but through His great mercies, so shall He have mercy on him.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 12:24: The particulars of trust are many, and this is but a small gleaning from what the pious one explained in Chovot HaLevavot (Gate of Trust). And in general, one who trusts is fittingly called "chassid," and is a chariot for the attribute of Chesed, like Abraham - for just as the pious one is called a lover, and it is the way of the lover to be cleaved in love of the Creator, as he says (Proverbs 18:24), "and there is a lover who cleaves closer than a brother," as we elaborated in the previous chapters, and he loves none besides the Creator - so the one who trusts does not trust in created beings, nor place the strength of his affairs upon them, but only upon the Creator. It follows that since his trust in Him is a cleaving to Him, he is a lover of Him - and this is what is explained in Chovot HaLevavot, peace be upon him, that one who trusts is fitting to give himself over to His judgment, like Abraham our father when he was cast into the fiery furnace, and likewise the matter of Chananya, Mishael, and Azaryah, and so on - and we copied his words above (chapter 6).
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 12:25: And so you find concerning Abraham our father, peace be upon him, that he was tested with ten trials, and were it not for his trust in the Creator, blessed be He, and his strength in the cords of his love, he would have rebelled; and it is written (Nehemiah 9:8), "and found his heart faithful before You" - "faithful" [ne'eman] means strong and enduring, unshakeable - and this is the explanation of "ne'eman" found throughout the Torah, such as (1 Kings 11:38), "and I will build for you a sure [ne'eman] house," and the opposite of this (Genesis 45:26), "and his heart fainted, for he did not believe them." And so concerning the fulfillment and strength of a statement, it is said (Numbers 5:22), "and the woman shall say, Amen, Amen." And there is no need to elaborate further on this, for it is simple.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 12:26: It follows that the believer and the truster are both one matter - for the truster too has his heart supported and steadfast concerning the desired thing, in the One who will fulfill it for him, as explained above. And I found written that it is impossible to be a truster if one is not a believer, and faith in God, blessed be He, is what brings him to trust - for since he believes in the Creator, blessed be He, he understands that his success, whether in this world or the World to Come, all comes from Him, and there is none other besides Him - then he sets his heart to trust in Him and to love Him with all his heart.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 12:27: And the thing that brings a person to be a believer is that he not fear any evil thing, but accept everything that comes upon him with joy - and he is like a servant who knows his master to be generous and good of eye, and at the time he imposes hard labor upon his servants, he then does them great good, elevates them and raises them up, and they become his counselors, eating from his table, riding in his second chariot, and appointed over his treasury. And without doubt, this servant, knowing and recognizing this about his master, will abandon everything in the world in order to do his master's will with joy - and even though that labor is very hard for him to perform, in remembering the good that will come to him because of that labor, everything becomes easy for him. But a servant who sees his master as stingy, and his toil greater than his wage, toils only in sorrow. So it is with this matter: for one who truly believes that everything he does and labors for in the service of the Creator is all for his own good, and the Holy One, blessed be He, will give him a great and good reward for everything he endures for His great Name, and for all the service and ministration he performs for the sake of Heaven He will give him pleasantness in the World to Come - along the lines of what we find concerning Nebuchadnezzar, that for four steps he took in honor of the Creator he merited great greatness in this world (Sanhedrin 96a); and also Esau, for honoring his father and mother, merited greatness in this world, he and his seed after him; and so many similar cases. And there is no doubt that when a person believes all this with a whole heart, he will certainly rejoice in all of God's judgments - for who would not rejoice, giving a penny to charity for the sake of Heaven, and being given in exchange for it, in the World to Come, a talent of gold?
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 12:28: And whoever believes in God with a whole heart will believe in the punishment of the sinner, and will not come to sin - and therefore the whole Torah depends on faith. How so? The beginning of the Torah is (Exodus 20:2), "I am the LORD your God," "you shall have no other gods before Me" - and if he does not believe, what use is his Torah to him? And when a person believes from the depths of his heart that the Creator will fulfill everything written in His Torah, to punish the sinner - and He is a witness - and brings good reward to whoever fulfills His Torah, then he keeps the Torah - for if the thief and the robber knew that they would be killed and would not escape, they would restrain themselves from theft and robbery, but they think and trust that they will be saved - and therefore the whole Torah is entirely bound up with faith, as it is written (Habakkuk 2:4), "but the righteous shall live by his faith," and of Abraham it is said (Genesis 15:6), "and he believed in the LORD, and He counted it to him as righteousness" - and concerning all the rest that he did, "righteousness" is not written, but only concerning his faith. And concerning this it is said (Numbers 12:7), "he is faithful in all My house."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 12:29: And I further say, that all the commandments that depend on tradition require faith - and if he does not believe, he destroys the whole Torah; for if he does not believe that this is the Torah of Moses given to us, and likewise in the tradition of the Scribes who so explained the commandments of sukkah and lulav and the like, then he denies the Torah. Similarly with matters we have by tradition, that our Rabbis, of blessed memory, mentioned in Tractate Berachot (54a) - one who sees the stone on which Moses sat, and the fords of the Jordan, or the place of the altar Elijah made on Carmel - for all these matters depend on tradition, and likewise that this is the Temple and this is Jerusalem and the like - all these require faith; and if he believes in these, his soul will be inflamed with love of the Creator when he remembers the miracles He performed for us in those places, but if he does not believe, certainly he has no love for the Creator.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 12:30: And they said in the Midrash, brought in the Yalkut (Parashat Beshalach, section 240, page 69c), on the verse "and they believed in the LORD, and in Moses His servant," "and they believed in the LORD" - as a reward for the faith they believed, the holy spirit rested upon them and they said song, as it is written (Exodus 15:1), "then Moses and the children of Israel sang." Rabbi Nechemiah says, from where do you say that whoever accepts upon himself even one commandment in faith is worthy of having the holy spirit rest upon him? For so we find our fathers, as a reward for the faith they believed, and so on - you find that our fathers were redeemed from Egypt only in the merit of faith, as it is said (Exodus 4:31), "and the people believed" - and so it says (Psalms 31:24), "the LORD preserves the faithful."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 12:31: And further he says: this is the gate of the LORD, the righteous shall enter through it (ibid. 118:20) - concerning the masters of faith, what does it say (Isaiah 26:2)? "Open the gates, that the righteous nation which keeps faith may enter" - through this gate all the masters of faith enter. And so it says (Psalms 92:2), "it is good to give thanks to the LORD" - what brought them to this joy, if not the reward of the faith their fathers believed in this world, which is entirely night? Therefore it is said (ibid. 92:3), "to declare Your kindness in the morning," and so on. And so Jehoshaphat says to the people (2 Chronicles 20:20), "believe in the LORD your God, so shall you be established; believe His prophets, so shall you prosper." "O LORD, are Your eyes not upon faithfulness?" (Jeremiah 5:3); "but the righteous shall live by his faith" (Habakkuk 2:4); "they are new every morning, great is Your faithfulness" (Lamentations 3:23). And so you find that the exiles are gathered in only as a reward for faith, as it is said (Song of Songs 4:8), "with me from Lebanon, my bride," and so on, "look from the top of Amanah," "and I will betroth you to Me forever; and I will betroth you to Me in faithfulness" (Hosea 2:21-22) - behold, how great is faith before Him who spoke and the world came into being, that as a reward for the faith they believed, the holy spirit rested upon them and they said song, as it is said (Exodus 14:31), "and they believed in the LORD, and in Moses His servant... then sang Moses," and so it says (Psalms 106:12), "then they believed His words; they sang His praise" - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 12:32: And the reason faith is attributed to Chesed - we have already copied at the beginning of the chapter the words of the Tikkunim (page 5a), that they said that in it is the Shema, which is faith. And the intent is that of the four passages in the tefillin, the third passage is Chesed, and in the third passage we mention the faith of unity, "the LORD our God, the LORD is One" - and so Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained (Parashat Bo, page 43b), whose words we copied above in chapter 5, where he said: the third passage, "Shema," is the secret of the right, called supernal Chesed, which unifies the unity of all in four directions, and the Holy One, blessed be He, arranges through it the order of the whole world, and this is what spreads even into the lower depths - to this point. And through the Chesed that spreads into all created beings, as he said that it spreads even into the depths, created beings believe in Him and in His unity - therefore the word "emunah," first mentioned in the Torah, is mentioned concerning Abraham, as it is said, "and he believed in the LORD" - through Abraham, true faith was revealed in the world, as explained in the Zohar, that Abraham our father, peace be upon him, would make known to all who came into the world that there is a Creator who created everything and whose kindness is present to all.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 12:33: And through this may be understood what they said in the Zohar (end of Parashat Vayelech), that one who answers "Amen" to every single blessing - just as he thereby opens the supernal gates, the gates of the supernal flow, so they will open for his soul when it departs this world, as it is said (Isaiah 26:2), "open the gates, that the righteous nation which keeps faith [shomer emunim] may enter" - do not read "emunim" but "amenim." And the reason is that the opening of the gates is from the side of Chesed, as explained in the Tikkunim (page 38b), "open for me on the first day," and so too the opening indicated by the vowel points is Chochmah, as explained in the Tikkunim (page 128) - and reason dictates that the King opens gates only from the side of His great kindness and simple will, for from the side of judgment the flow would be closed, and through Chesed it is opened - and this is "You open Your hand" - and since one who answers Amen opens the gates through Chesed, it is fitting that gates be opened for him in the future.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 12:34: It follows that through His flowing of kindness to us, we fix our faith in Him - and this is what Scripture says (Lamentations 3:23), "they are new every morning, great is Your faithfulness" - for through the kindness He performs with us every morning, in that we deposit with Him the weary soul, and He returns it to us new, and all that weariness it had is gone, and it is a new soul as at the beginning of its creation - behold, this is a great kindness, and this renewal is certainly from the side of Chesed, for the meaning of "who renews in His goodness, every single day, continually, the work of creation" (the Yotzer Or blessing) - and especially in the mornings, which is the "morning of Abraham" (Zohar, Parashat Mishpatim, page 119b). Through this, "great is Your faithfulness" - we have great faith afterward to deposit our souls in His hand every night, in remembering the kindness He does with us.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 12:35: And let us return to the exposition we were engaged in, that trust and faith are partners with one another - for whoever believes in God with a whole heart will trust in Him with a strong trust, and trust will bring him not to fear anything, and not to serve any person besides the Creator, for He is God, and not to hope in any man, nor agree with them in anything contrary to the service of God, and their affairs will not frighten him, nor will he fear their disputes; and if he rebukes them, he will not be careful of their honor, nor be ashamed of them, nor beautify falsehood for them - as the prophet said (Isaiah 50:7), "for the Lord GOD will help me; therefore I am not confounded." And his trust will bring him to turn away from the affairs of the world and to unify his heart to the matters of Torah and service - and this is possible only if his trust is great in YHVH, and therefore his reward is great, that he be bound in Chesed, as it is written (Psalms 32:10), "but he who trusts in the LORD, kindness shall surround him." And it says "shall surround him" - meaning, Chesed shall encircle him and clothe him, along the lines of (Exodus 21:8), "he shall have no power to sell her to a foreign people, seeing he has dealt deceitfully with her" - which is explained in the Sabba (page 96b) as fine garments from the side of the name "Eloah," which is Chesed. And the reason he says "in YHVH" is that YHVH is the root of all the [divine] names and all the modes of existence, and since he places his trust in the essence of all, who sustains all and brings into being it, its spirit, and its soul, he is removed from all the mishaps of the world, and Chesed conceals him from all the masters of judgment, as he says (Psalms 91:2-4), "I will say of the LORD, He is my refuge and my fortress... for He shall deliver you from the snare of the fowler," and so on, "He shall cover you with His pinions, and under His wings shall you take refuge," and so on.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 12:36: And among the conditions of the faithful and the truster is to be faithful in his service to the Creator, like a peg fixed in a faithful place that will not slip - for the Holy One, blessed be He, is called "the faithful God, who keeps the covenant and kindness," and so on (Deuteronomy 7:9), and His kindness is forever spread to all creatures, and it cannot be conceived that His kindness would slip from His creatures, Heaven forfend, and cease in a moment - rather, the Holy One, blessed be He, made a covenant and a statute in His kindness with His creatures, that His kindness never depart from them - and this is why we find in the Torah "covenant" adjacent to "kindness," along the lines of (Deuteronomy 7:12), "the LORD your God shall keep with you the covenant and the kindness," and so the prophet said (Isaiah 54:10), "for the mountains shall depart," and so on, "but My kindness shall not depart from you, nor shall My covenant of peace be removed," and so on. It follows that whoever is faithful in his words, his commandments, and his Torah is bound to Chesed and to Tzedek [righteousness] as one.
